On 21 August 1959 Hawaii became the 50th state of the United States, after a vote in which most residents backed statehood.

Hawaii had been a US territory since annexation in 1898, after the overthrow. Its large Asian American population, many descended from Japanese and other plantation workers, had faced doubts in Congress; their service in the Second World War helped change minds.

Statehood came with jet travel, and tourism soon replaced sugar as the main business. Native Hawaiians later pointed out that the 1959 vote offered no option of independence.
sum: On 21 August 1959 Hawaii became the 50th state of the United States, after a vote in which most residents backed statehood.
